summary: The Petitioner, NTPC Ltd. (“Petitioner”/ “NTPC”), has filed the present Petition under Section 79 (1) (a) & (k) read with Section 62 of the Electricity Act, 2003 (“the Act”), seeking expenditure towards procurement and capitalization of wagons for Kahalgaon Super Thermal Power Station, Stage-I (840 MW) (“Kahalgaon-I”) located in the State of Bihar. The Petitioner has made the following prayers: - _c) Pass any other order as it may deem fit in the circumstances mentioned above._ 2. The Petitioner is a Government Company within the meaning of the Companies Act, 1956 and a ‘Generating Company’ as defined under Section 2(28) of the Electricity Act, 2003 (the Act). It operates power stations and projects across various regions of the country, including Kahalgaon-I, located in the State of Bihar. 30.7.2016 in Petition No. 279/GT/2014. The Petitioner further referred to a similar _Order in Petition No.424/MP/2025 Page_ _**3** of 20_ disallowance in Petition No. 150/2009 (Farakka STPS), which was upheld by the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (APTEL) in its order dated 26.3.2014 in Appeal No. 86 of 2012. However, the Hon’ble Supreme Court, in Civil Appeal No. 5990 of 2014, by judgment dated 9.11.2017, set aside the APTEL order and remanded the matter to the APTEL for reconsideration. 6. The Petitioner, in support of the relief sought, has mainly submitted the following: - (f) The Commission has duly recognised the necessity of wagons for the generating station in question and has not disallowed the Petitioner’s claim on this ground. It has appropriately granted the Petitioner liberty to approach the Commission upon the final adjudication by the APTEL in the remand proceedings concerning Farakka STPS. The Commission, in a similar context, 7. Notices were issued to the Respondents to file their replies. The Petitioner vide ROP dated 24.6.2025 was directed to file certain additional information, _inter alia_ , regarding the capitalization of 10 wagons, their availability, and status, decapitalization of unserviceable wagons, and requisite certifications, including non-duplication of claims and compliance with the prescribed SoP. In compliance with the Commission’s directions, the Petitioner filed the requisite additional information vide affidavit dated 6.8.2025. Respondent No. 1, BSPHCL, filed its Reply vide affidavit dated 25.8.2025, and the Petitioner submitted its Rejoinder vide affidavit dated 9.9.2025. 8. BSPHCL, in response to the main Petition and additional information submitted by the Petitioner, has submitted as follows: - - (a) That the present Petition has been filed by the Petitioner pursuant to the liberty granted in the order dated 19.5.2024 in Petition No. 294/GT/2020, _Order in Petition No.424/MP/2025 Page_ _**8** of 20_ (b) BSPHCL's assertion that liberty to approach does not create a vested right is a misreading of the order. The liberty granted by the Commission is a binding procedural safeguard, ensuring that NTPC’s legitimate claim, otherwise deferred, could be agitated once the appellate ruling was delivered. The APTEL judgment, being final and binding on identical issues, establishes the legitimacy of capitalization of wagons. Hence, the present Petition squarely falls within the protective ambit of the Commission’s order and Regulation 14(3)(x) of the 2014 Tariff Regulations. (d) The suggestion that the Petitioner bears the burden of strict proof and has not produced contemporaneous evidence is factually incorrect. The Petition is supported by audited accounts, station records, Form-9Bi, additional submissions dated 10.5.2022 in Petition No. 294/GT/2020, and the Auditor’s certification confirming both capitalization and corresponding decapitalization of old wagons. These constitute contemporaneous and verifiable records, fully satisfying the prudence check envisaged under the Regulations. - (o) The overarching suggestion that the Petition is not bona fide is a bald and unfounded allegation. The Petition arises from liberty granted by the Commission itself, is supported by binding precedent of the APTEL, and is backed by audited financials, statutory records, and prudence check disclosures. The Petition is thus fully maintainable and meritorious. 10. The matter was heard on 26.9.2025. Based on the request of learned counsels of the parties, the Petitioner and Respondent were permitted to file their respective written submissions, with a copy to the opposite side. Subject thereto, the order in the Petition was reserved. Thereafter, the Petitioner and BSPHCL, vide affidavits dated 13.10.2025, filed their written submissions reiterating the averments made in the Petition, Reply, and Rejoinder; hence, the same are not being repeated for the sake of brevity. 11.
